children: Elara Securities initiates coverage with a Buy rating and a Rs 1,367 target price, citing rising ARPU, digital services growth and AirFiber expansion

Brokerage Elara Securities has initiated coverage of Jio Platforms with a ‘Buy’ rating and a target price of Rs 1,367, implying an upside of 22 per cent from the final issue price of Rs 1,119. The brokerage expects the Reliance Industries subsidiary to strengthen its position as a digital services provider, supported by affordable data, rising average revenue per user (ARPU) and expanding home broadband connections.

In its research report dated 28 October 2026, Elara Securities projected Jio Platforms’ revenue to grow at a CAGR of 13 per cent between FY26 and FY29, while earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) are expected to rise at a CAGR of 16 per cent. Profit after tax (PAT) is forecast to grow at a faster CAGR of 23 per cent over the same period.
The brokerage has based its target price on 11.5 times estimated FY29 Ebitda. It also cautioned that the valuation and recommendation may be reviewed following price discovery when the shares list.
Digital Services Emerge As A Long-Term Growth Driver

Elara Securities sees digital products and services as an important long-term growth opportunity for Jio Platforms, although the business currently contributes a relatively small share of overall revenue.

Digital services accounted for around 12 per cent of revenue in FY26, according to the report. The brokerage expects the business to expand as Jio leverages its large customer base and distribution network to offer consumer and enterprise services, including cloud computing, communications, productivity tools, artificial intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT).

The report estimates that digital products and services revenue will grow at a CAGR of around 23 per cent between FY26 and FY29, while Ebitda is expected to increase at a CAGR of approximately 36 per cent. Its contribution to revenue is projected to rise to around 16 per cent by FY29.
Elara Securities believes affordable connectivity, combined with a wider portfolio of digital offerings, will help Jio improve customer engagement and monetisation beyond its core telecom business.
Tariff Hikes And Premium Plans To Support ARPU Growth

Mobile services are expected to remain Jio Platforms’ primary revenue and profitability driver in the near term. The brokerage anticipates a tariff increase of 12–15 per cent from the second half of FY27, alongside continued subscriber additions and migration towards higher-value plans.
Jio’s ARPU is projected to rise from Rs 214 in FY26 to Rs 257 in FY29, representing a CAGR of around 6 per cent.

Other factors expected to support ARPU growth include migration from 2G to 4G and 5G networks, a shift from prepaid to postpaid plans, higher data consumption and the adoption of bundled digital services.
Elara Securities expects Jio’s mobile subscriber base to increase from 524 million in FY26 to 573 million by FY29, implying a CAGR of around 3 per cent.

However, the brokerage expects Jio to retain a pricing advantage over Bharti Airtel, even as it gradually increases tariffs. It noted that Jio’s ARPU stood at Rs 216 in the first quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 264 for Airtel.
Home Broadband And AirFiber Offer Significant Upside
Home broadband is another major growth opportunity identified in the report, given India’s relatively low fixed broadband penetration and the increasing adoption of fixed wireless access (FWA).

Elara Securities expects Jio Platforms’ fixed broadband subscriber base to grow from 27 million in FY26 to 66 million by FY29, representing a CAGR of around 35 per cent. JioAirFiber is projected to account for approximately 80 per cent of incremental broadband additions during the period.

The brokerage highlighted Jio’s proprietary unlicensed band radio (UBR) technology and its established position in FWA as competitive advantages, particularly in areas where fibre deployment is expensive or difficult.
Jio held around 43 per cent of India’s fixed broadband market in the first quarter of FY27 and approximately 79 per cent of the 5G- and UBR-based FWA segment, according to the report.

The company’s ambition to reach 100 million home broadband connections could provide further scope for growth as household adoption increases and customers move towards premium plans and bundled entertainment services.
Key Risks Include Delayed Tariff Increases
Elara Securities identified delays in tariff hikes as a key downside risk to its projections, as slower price increases could affect revenue and Ebitda growth.
The possible imposition of spectrum charges on UBR technology or other regulatory levies could also increase costs and affect the expansion of fixed broadband services.
Despite these risks, the brokerage believes Jio Platforms is positioned to benefit from rising data consumption, greater 5G adoption and the expansion of India’s digital services market.
The report forecasts Ebitda margins to improve from 50 per cent in FY26 to 53.8 per cent in FY29, supported by operating leverage and a growing contribution from higher-value services.

Elara Securities’ investment thesis rests on Jio Platforms’ ability to move beyond connectivity towards a broader digital ecosystem, with mobile services providing near-term growth and digital products and home broadband creating additional monetisation opportunities over the longer term.
